questions.stem: A 51-year-old woman complained to her gynecologist of persistent vaginal burning and vaginal pain during intercourse. One year earlier, the woman had undergone a total hysterectomy because of a large leiomyoma. Physical examination showed dryness and atrophy of the vagina. A vaginal cream was prescribed. Which of the following drugs would be appropriate for local therapy in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ethinylestradiol
  • Total hysterectomy includes the removal of the ovaries.
  • Vaginal dryness and atrophy due to estrogen deficiency is a common causes of dyspareunia (painful vaginal intercourse) and can be cured with estrogen administration.
  • Topical forms of estrogens (creams, vaginal tablets, etc.) are as effective as or more effective than oral forms for this indication and are usually preferred.
  • When estrogen cream is used, women with a uterus are also given a progestin(to prevent endometrial hyperplasia), which is not needed following a hysterectomy, as in this case.
  • SERMs like ospemifene are also used in the treatment of atrophic vaginitis.

questions.stem: During her annual checkup, a 32-year-old woman was found to have mild hypertension (160/90 mm Hg). The woman, otherwise healthy, had started an oral contraceptive (ethinyl estradiol and norgestrel) 2 months earlier. The physician decided to change her contraceptive pill and prescribed ethinyl estradiol and drospirenone. Increased excretion of which of the following ions most likely occurred in this patient after a few days of therapy?
questions.solutionHtml:
Sodium
  • Drospirenone-It is structurally related to spironolactone and acts as an aldosterone receptor antagonist.
  • Therefore, it causes an increased renal sodium excretion, which can account for its diuretic and antihypertensive effects.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman asked her physician for a postcoital contraceptive 2 days following unprotected intercourse. Which of the following drugs would be most appropriate for this purpose?
questions.solutionHtml:
Levonorgestrel
  • Levonorgestrel, a progestin compound, is an effective postcoital contraceptive.
  • The effectiveness is most likely due to a combination of effects of interaction with progesterone receptors and the time of the cycle.
  • Among the contraceptive actions are inhibition of ovulation, alterations in cervical mucus production, and decreased fallopian tube motility, all of which can hinder fertilization and/or disrupt the development of an endometrium suitable for implantation.
  • It can be given up to 72 hrs after unprotected

questions.stem: A 59-year-old woman diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer started a treatment that included anastrozole. Which of the following molecular actions most likely mediated the therapeutic effect of the drug in the patient’s disease?

options.label: D
options.text: Inhibition of conversion of androgens to estrogens

questions.answerText: Inhibition of conversion of androgens to estrogens
questions.solutionHtml:
Inhibition of conversion of androgens to estrogens
  • Aromatase inhibitors are considered second-line agents for hormone-dependent breast cancers, but they are increasingly used in this disease in postmenopausal women, in whom they cause an almost total suppression of estrogen synthesis.
  • Anastrozole and letrozole are selective inhibitors of aromatase, the enzyme responsible for the conversion of androgens to estrogens, including the extra-adrenal synthesis of estrogen from androstenedione, which takes place in several tissues, including the breast.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman had been taking a combined oral contraceptive pill for the past 5 years. However, she recently developed a disorder that prompted her physician to withdraw the pill and recommend other forms of contraception. Which of the following disorders most likely occurred to this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Vein thrombosis
  • Thromboembolic disease is an absolute contraindication for the use of a combined oral contraceptive pill.
  • The estrogen component of OCPs has been mainly held responsible for venous thromboembolism, while both estrogen and progestin have been blamed for the arterial phenomena.

The mechanisms involved may be

  • Increase in blood clotting factors (coagulability is enhanced)
  • Decreased antithrombin III
  • Decreased plasminogen activator in endothelium
  • Increased platelet aggregation
  • Progestin-only contraceptives may be used in women with thromboembolic In such cases; IUCDs are preferred.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man with a long history of chronic cardiac failure presented to his physician complaining of urinary hesitancy and frequent need to urinate during the night. An examination revealed an enlarged prostate and further exams confirmed the diagnosis of benign prostatic hyperplasia. Finasteride was included as part of his therapeutic regimen. Which of the following actions most likely mediated the therapeutic effect of the drug in the patient’s disease?

options.label: A
options.text: Inhibition of follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) and luteinizing hormone (LH) release

questions.solutionHtml:
Inhibition of 5α-reductase enzyme
  • Finasteride is a competitive inhibitor of 5α-reductase, the enzyme that converts testosterone to dihydrotestosterone.
  • Finasteride blocks only type 1 of the 5-α-reductase enzyme.
  • Dutasteride blocks both types 1 and 2 of the 5-α-reductase enzyme.

Uses of Finasteride-

  • Benign prostatic hyperplasia
  • Hirsutism
  • Male pattern baldness

questions.stem: A 54-year-old woman presented to her physician complaining of hot flashes and night sweats that disturbed her sleep. Her last menstrual period was 6 months ago. The physician prescribed a hormone replacement therapy with a combined contraceptive pill (ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone). This therapy might carry a small increase in the risk of which of the following diseases?
questions.solutionHtml:
Breast cancer
  • Hormone replacement therapy is the most effective treatment option for alleviating vasomotor symptoms (hot flushes and night sweats) in postmenopausal women. The risk of malignant tumors in women taking hormonal contraceptives is probably the major concern for the use of these medications in perimenopausal women.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman asked her physician for a contraceptive pill. Because the woman had suffered in the past from deep venous thrombosis, the physician prescribed a progestin-only oral contraceptive (the mini pill). Which of the following actions most likely contributed to the contraceptive effect of the prescribed drug?

options.label: A
options.text: Activation of progestin receptors in the corpus luteum

options.label: B
options.text: Stimulation of follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) release from the pituitary

options.label: C
options.text: Increased viscosity of the cervical mucus

options.label: D
options.text: Increased frequency of gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) pulse generator

questions.answerText: Increased viscosity of the cervical mucus
questions.solutionHtml:
Increased viscosity of the cervical mucus
  • In patients with Venous thromboembolism, IUCD is a contraceptive of choice.
  • Among the oral contraceptives-Progestin-only pills(mini-pills) can be used.
  • These pills increase the viscosity of cervical mucus, which decreases sperm penetration

questions.stem: A 21-year-old woman complained to her physician of recurrent nausea lasting most of the day. The woman had been suffering from a urinary tract infection presently being treated with ciprofloxacin and from gastroesophageal reflux disease presently being treated with omeprazole. She also routinely took ibuprofen during her menstrual period. One week ago, she started taking a contraceptive pill (ethinyl estradiol and norgestrel). Which of the following drugs most likely caused the patient’s nausea?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ethinyl estradiol
  • Nausea from a combined oral contraceptive can generally be attributed to the estrogen component (ethinyl estradiol).
  • It was a common adverse effect and was one of the main reasons for discontinuing the use of combined contraceptives.
  • Today, with the use of low-dose contraceptive pills, this adverse effect is much less common.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old woman requests birth control. She has no medical conditions, and she smokes one pack of Cigarettes per day. Which would be the most appropriate to recommend?
questions.solutionHtml:
Progestin-only “mini-pill”
  • Progestin-only products are preferred in older women who are smokers, due to a lower risk of severe adverse effects, such as myocardial infarction and Estrogen-containing contraceptives are not recommended in women over the age of 35 who are smokers.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man with a history of myocardial infarction and angina has a prescription for sublingual Nitroglycerine but has not taken it. He now complains of erectile dysfunction and is given a prescription for Sildenafil 50 mg. He is warned by his physician not to take sildenafil and nitroglycerine because of which of the following possible reactions?
questions.solutionHtml:
Hypotension
  • Nitrate+PDE 5 inhibitors (Sildenafil )→ Increased cGMP→
  • Vasodilation→Hypotension, Increased Heart rate, Myocardial Infarction.
  • Hypotension is most common among these drug interaction reactions.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old female came to the gynecology OPD with C/O not being able to conceive even after 2 years of unprotected sexual intercourse. The doctor decided to induce ovulation for her by giving Clomiphene citrate. How should the drug be given to this patient?
